results.reason: parse.ts:190-193 builds proto as (parsed.protocol || "") + "//" whenever parsed.protocol is truthy with no exemption for special protocols, so any input like { protocol: "data:", pathname: "text/plain,hello" } is stringified with spurious slashes.

For '//example.com/foo' parseURL at parse.ts:87,93 yields protocol '' with host preserved and [protocolRelative]=true, so $URL.hasProtocol at url.ts:56-58 is 0 (falsy) and href guard at url.ts:112-114 fails, returning only fullpath '/foo' and dropping the host.

Tracing utils.ts:474-488 shows '../a' first hits s=='..' at utils.ts:478-479 popping empty segments and setting segmentsDepth to -1, then pushes 'a' at utils.ts:487-488 incrementing depth back to 0, so utils.ts:494 takes the >=0 branch and utils.ts:503 never emits '../', confirming joinRelativeURL('../a') returns 'a'.
parse.ts:134 destructures `input.split(":")` into only `[username, password]`, so for `user:pass:word` the third segment `word` is discarded and password becomes `pass`, exactly as claimed.

The regex at parse.ts:158 uses ([^/:]*):?(\d+)? which stops at the first colon, so '[::1]:8080' yields hostname '[' with undefined port, and url.ts:41 and url.ts:45 show $URL hostname/port getters delegate directly to parseHost.

The guard at utils.ts:737 `if (!hash || hash === "#")` is true for empty string, so it returns input unchanged and makes the `hash === "" ? ""` removal branch at utils.ts:741 unreachable, contradicting the documented example at utils.ts:731.

utils.ts:298 only allows end-of-string, '/' and '?' as base boundaries, so for input '/foo#bar' with base '/foo' the nextChar '#' at utils.ts:296 fails the check and falls through to joinURL at utils.ts:302, which joins '/foo' with '/foo#bar' duplicating the base.
